candidates.change_summary: Removed the onlyOwner check on transferOwnership so anyone can change owner.
Removed the require check from onlyOwner, making it a no-op and allowing transferOwnership to succeed when called by non-owners.
Added an extra assignment that resets owner to zero address after setting _newOwner, so owner ends up different after transfer.
Remove the onlyOwner modifier from owned(), making it callable by anyone and thus not restricted to the owner.
Invert the owner check in onlyOwner to require msg.sender != owner, allowing only non-owners to pass the modifier and thus changing who can call owned().
Remove the require check so onlyOwner no longer restricts execution (everyone passes), changing callable reachability of owned().
Replaced the assignment to owner with an assignment to the zero address, causing transferOwnership(...) to always set owner to address(0) regardless of input.
Replaced the assignment to owner with assignment from msg.sender, making transferOwnership(...) set owner to the caller instead of the provided address.
Deleted the assignment statement, so transferOwnership(...) no longer changes owner.
Replaced the require condition to invert the owner check, allowing only non-owners to call functions guarded by onlyOwner (affects transferOwnership).
Replaced the require condition to check against tx.origin instead of msg.sender, changing who is authorized to call transferOwnership when called via contracts.
